newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps edge higher, bar jet front months.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps edge higher, bar jet front months.

text.p: European oil swaps edged tentatively higher on Tuesday tracking firmer oil futures.

CFDs made ground while gasoline recovered some of the losses from the morning. The gas oil crack widened and the tone, if not the price, of heavy fuel firmed. Jet front month swaps slipped about $1, although 4Q and 1Q held.

Brent CFDs gained 10 cents a barrel to 90 cents under June for the balance of the week, although most talk had moved on to next week where 66.50 cents under compared with 74 cents under in the morning.
The following two weeks until the end of April showed gains of a touch under 10 cents at 55 cents and 8 cents for the final April week at 49 cents under.
Gas oil crack spreads against Brent firmed with stronger bidding in the afternoon pushing values higher. Traders said 3Q rose to $4.35 a barrel from $4.30 in the morning while 4Q held at $4.85.
Buying interest into 1998 was also evident with 1Q valued around $4.63 and 2Q at $4.10.
The strength reflected some airline buying and banks hedging on the crack. But the stronger bids were not always translating into done deals.
"We are getting better bids, but the offers are moving away," said one trader.

Airlines were seen picking up 4Q jet swaps at $207 cif NWE and 1Q at $205, but earlier months saw values slip by $1 or so with April premiums pegged at $23 a tonne above the IPE April gas oil and $24.25 above May.
Low sulphur fuel swaps activity was fairly muted with traders commenting on the high sulphur barge to low sulphur cargo spread being too narrow.

"It needs to widen out for more to happen (on low sulphur)," said one trader. Low sulphur cargo swaps were pegged steady at May $90.50. High sulphur fuel swaps were assessed as more bullish with April barges heard done at $85.25 and $85.50. But, activity was capped by the presence of more buyers than sellers.

Gasoline recovered some of the morning's losses with May talked at $194-$195. Physical deals were concluded at $190 for Eurograde in the morning and the same parties then traded at $183 in the afternoon for regular.
Gasoline swaps business was ticking along with a variety of sellers seeking to match with predominantly one buyer.
